learning_outcomes.text: To acquaint students with issues related to optimization and types of optimization
Mastering the skills associated with defining the optimization task
The use of software designed to optimize the structure
A student has knowledge including the ability to model machine construction, conduct numerical simulations and use numerical simulation software

Student can independently define the optimization task, build a mathematical model of the objective function and constraints. He can run optimization using software dedicated to it as well as use software for numerical calculations. He can interpret the results of optimization.
learning_outcomes.code: K_UW02, K_UW03, K_UW04, K_UW10, K_UK16, K_U18

learning_outcomes.text: A student is able to cooperate and work in a group and understands the non-technical aspects of the engineer-mechanic activity, including the impact on the environment and safety

syllabus_topics: Presentation of mathematical foundations in structural optimization
Examples of the use of optimization in issues not related to the optimization of the structure
Presentation of the method of optimal construction design using strength criteria
Definition of optimization task: objective function, limitations
Solving optimization tasks in numerical calculation software
The use of software for numerical calculations in optimization
A stand-alone solution for a single and multidimensional project
Designing a structure/frame that meets the limitations imposed during the classes
Manual optimization of the designed structure
Optimization with using the software to find the optimal geometry
A definition of optimization areas and areas separated from optimization
Definition of new geometry after topological optimization. With use of the dedicated software
Manufacturability on an example of the geometry from the topological optimization
assessment_rules: The condition for passing the course is to achieve all the required learning outcomes specified for the course. The final grade is calculated based on the average of the student's grades from the in-class test for lectures and from the projects/exercises for the lab.
